summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, polymyositis, interstitial lung disease, type 2 diabetes, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and recurrent venous thromboembolism was admitted for a left thigh abscess with fever and pain. She underwent two incision and drainage procedures after imaging confirmed a persistent fluid collection. Treatment included intravenous antibiotics, later transitioned to oral Augmentin and Bactrim. During her stay, she was found to have a polymyositis flare with elevated CK, managed with IV and then oral steroids, tapering to 10 mg prednisone. Her warfarin had been stopped prior to admission due to heavy menstrual bleeding, leading to a subtherapeutic INR; it was restarted and increased to 7 mg daily. Acute on chronic heart failure was managed with a short course of IV furosemide. Vaginal bleeding was evaluated with a normal pelvic ultrasound and attributed to PCOS or fibroids, possibly exacerbated by anticoagulation. She improved clinically, with normalizing labs, and was discharged home on a completed antibiotic course, adjusted anticoagulation, and rheumatology follow-up for immunosuppressive medication reinitiation.
problems: Cutaneous abscess of left lower limb
Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
